policy: Limits may stay fixed or decrease. Raising one requires an explicit performance-regression review in the pull request.

reviewedExceptions.change: Lazy-load Settings and consolidate shared modules
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept about 0.14% more total JavaScript bookkeeping in exchange for over 15% less startup JavaScript on both targets; the added bytes are not in the startup closure.

reviewedExceptions.change: Add lazy runtime performance instrumentation
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept about 0.41% more startup JavaScript and 0.55% more total JavaScript to collect privacy-safe streaming, composer, persistence, and memory-growth evidence. The 4.8–5.0 KB collector is lazy; startup carries only the ordering/provider bridge, whose direct loaded-path calls avoid per-delta closure and collection allocation.

reviewedExceptions.change: Remove the blocking Settings loading backdrop and animate first mount in CSS
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 474 Safari / 409 Chrome startup CSS bytes for first-mount entry keyframes while removing the JavaScript loading dialog. Combined startup JS plus CSS decreases by 220 bytes on Safari and 299 bytes on Chrome, and the full-screen first-open blackout is eliminated.

reviewedExceptions.change: Add the chat typeface selector and split Settings into interface vs system panes
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept about 0.45% more startup CSS and 0.05% more startup JavaScript for a typography choice that ships zero font files and makes no network calls. The startup stylesheet carries the family stacks, scoped chat declarations, and picker presentation; picker labels and descriptions stay in the lazy Settings JavaScript chunk, while the cards reuse existing effort-slider styles. All four stacks are system fonts, so there is no download, no FOUT and no layout-shifting swap at runtime.

reviewedExceptions.change: Harden bounded thread loading and durable local transcript recovery
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept about 0.27% more startup JavaScript and 0.22% more total JavaScript for archive-safe SQLite discovery, interrupted-tail recovery, deep stale-cursor recovery, complete paginated exports, and stale OpenAI rollout repair. The persistence changes remove full legacy transcript blobs—up to many megabytes—from ordinary page reads and saves under the shared database lock. Transcript export formatting is now lazy, keeping action-only work out of startup.

reviewedExceptions.change: Add project-specific chat-font defaults
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept less than 0.02% more startup JavaScript and 0.06% more total JavaScript for a validated, inheritable project chat-font override with live Settings preview. The picker metadata remains in the lazy Settings chunk, no font files or network requests are added, and startup carries only the persisted-value sanitizer plus the active-project shell selection.

reviewedExceptions.change: Keep Settings dropdowns above the fixed footer
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 140 lazy Settings JavaScript bytes on both targets to explicitly open every Settings-owned menu upward. App-entry, startup JavaScript, startup CSS, and runtime listener counts are unchanged; the fixed placement prevents overflow clipping without adding shared positioning logic.

reviewedExceptions.change: Add account-aware Claude model replacement and managed developer-runtime updates
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept about 0.53% more startup JavaScript, 0.34% more startup CSS, and 0.58% more total JavaScript for conservative live-model supersession, actionable update-required rows, one delayed and deduplicated non-blocking startup check, and official Claude Code/Codex update controls. The network/update implementation and full Updates UI remain outside the startup closure; a follow-up size review removed 801 Safari startup-JavaScript bytes and 1,239 shared CSS bytes before recording this exception.

reviewedExceptions.change: Harden managed developer-runtime updates after review
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 102 startup JavaScript bytes, 106 startup CSS bytes, and at most 575 total JavaScript bytes for truthful unavailable-runtime actions, accessible updater status output, resilient post-update refresh handling, and friendly labels for superseded saved models. App-entry size is unchanged and its limits are ratcheted down to the measured production sizes.

reviewedExceptions.change: Address second-pass runtime updater review findings
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 77 Safari / 49 Chrome startup and total JavaScript bytes to expose a persisted update-required model's current state to assistive technology and consistently preserve friendly fallback-model metadata. App-entry and CSS sizes remain unchanged.

reviewedExceptions.change: Keep the Claude catalog label clear of its refresh control
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 205 startup CSS bytes on both targets for a fixed refresh-button column, a 10-pixel safety gap, and deterministic single-line truncation at narrow widths. App-entry and JavaScript sizes are unchanged.

reviewedExceptions.change: Make thread images durable and move provider selection into the composer
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept about 0.08% more startup JavaScript and 0.09% more total JavaScript for restart-safe image preview authorization, durable on-disk copies of new image inputs, the provider/model split in every composer rail, and consistent Claude supersession in Settings. Interface-size presentation is isolated in the existing lazy Settings boundary; a follow-up size pass kept Safari startup CSS below its previous limit and limited the Chrome CSS increase to 27 bytes. Thread memory still stores image paths rather than bytes.

reviewedExceptions.change: Close second-pass attachment and model-picker review findings
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept about 0.13% more startup JavaScript and 0.09% more total JavaScript for truthful superseded-model state, runnable project-default selection, disabled-row keyboard recovery, explicit image-persistence failures, and native preview accessibility. The native copy path simultaneously removes a second full in-memory image buffer of up to 50 MB by streaming directly through the filesystem; CSS and thread-memory payloads are unchanged.

reviewedExceptions.change: Make sends wait for durable attachment preparation
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 648 Safari / 647 Chrome startup and total JavaScript bytes to display selected files immediately while preventing a quick Send from omitting a still-copying image or persisting its temporary source path. The wait exists only when attachment preparation is outstanding; ordinary composer sends add no asynchronous work, and CSS and thread-memory payloads are unchanged.

reviewedExceptions.change: Make the composer model and provider pickers legible and mutually exclusive
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept at most 476 startup JavaScript bytes and 306 startup CSS bytes for a consistently short Model label, a readable responsive model menu, and symmetric provider/model dismissal for pointer and keyboard activation. The dismissal listeners exist only while a picker is open, and the change adds no network, persistence, thread-loading, or transcript-memory work.

reviewedExceptions.change: Close post-merge composer picker review findings
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 62 Safari / 69 Chrome startup and total JavaScript bytes for immutable-path click dismissal and arrow-key mutual exclusion. This keeps self-replacing menu actions open without weakening outside keyboard dismissal, and fixes intermediate-width overflow with no CSS-size increase. No idle listeners, network, persistence, thread-loading, or transcript-memory work is added.

reviewedExceptions.change: Add native clone-parent selection and interactive subscription quota details
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept about 0.87% more startup JavaScript, 0.70% more startup CSS, and 0.54% more total JavaScript for an accessible, selectable Codex/Claude usage popover and safe native clone-parent selection with exact destination previews. This is measured feature overhead, not a speed improvement. Clone presentation stays in the lazy Settings boundary; the popover reuses existing usage snapshots, attaches global listeners only while open, and adds no network requests, provider processes, polling, streaming work, or thread-payload growth. Limits match measured production output without extra headroom.

reviewedExceptions.change: Add bounded paint-only smoothing to live assistant text
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 4,274 Safari / 4,204 Chrome lazy JavaScript bytes (about 0.30% total) for a 180 ms fade of newly appended text. App entry, startup JavaScript and startup CSS are unchanged. The controller stays in the lazy timeline chunk, keeps existing deferred Markdown and DOM geometry, adds no provider/persistence work, and bounds live work to eight groups, 64 ranges/color reads, and a small capped message snapshot. This is measured feature overhead, not a speed improvement. Large or complex messages, rewrites, selection, reduced motion and unsupported browsers use ordinary fully visible text. Limits match measured output with no extra headroom.

reviewedExceptions.change: Make live text fades gentler and uninterrupted
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 817 Safari / 747 Chrome lazy JavaScript bytes (under 0.06% total) for a softer 420 ms curve, fixed time buckets, preserved Markdown DOM at completion, and atomic range-budget fallback. App entry, startup JavaScript and startup CSS are unchanged. Live decoration remains bounded: 24 color/time groups, 64 ranges/color reads, and the original message/snapshot limits. Overflow skips new decoration without evicting representable in-flight fades; completed history creates no controller. This is measured visual-feature overhead, not a speed improvement. No token queue, provider, persistence, thread-loading or transcript-memory changes are introduced. Limits match measured output with no extra headroom.

reviewedExceptions.change: Pace bursty streaming presentation before Markdown layout
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 3,084 Safari / 2,882 Chrome total JavaScript bytes for bounded display-only pacing and safe immediate code-copy flush. Most code remains lazy; shared React export bookkeeping adds 66 startup bytes and 59 app-entry bytes on each target. CSS is unchanged. This is measured visual-feature overhead, not an efficiency claim: paced live messages have more small renders, limited near 30 Hz with 240 ms arrival windows, 64 batches, 2,048 pending units and 48,000 source units. Provider/store/persistence text is not delayed. The captured Haiku replay shows smaller text/scroll/brightness steps; these are fixture results, not universal bounds or proof of subjective smoothness. Limits match measured output without headroom.

reviewedExceptions.change: Usage countdown and restrained toolbar presentation
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept the measured UI-feature cost of safe timezone-aware Claude reset-label parsing, a minute clock mounted only in open five-hour usage details, friendly Claude trigger names, and action feedback moved out of the fixed-width status text into existing toasts. No dependencies, extra provider reads, transcript changes or closed-panel timers. DST gaps/folds retain absolute labels rather than guessing. Most added JavaScript is shared parsing logic; total raw JS grows by 2,355 Safari / 2,300 Chrome bytes, with 223 startup CSS bytes for subdued selection and neutral notifications. This is feature overhead, not an efficiency claim. Exact measured limits, no extra headroom.

reviewedExceptions.change: Fade usage details and remove the first Settings Suspense retry delay
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 2,350 Safari / 2,130 Chrome startup and total JavaScript bytes, plus 53 CSS bytes, for interruptible opacity-only usage-panel presence, a stable asynchronous Settings host, and keyboard-accessible close/retry recovery for failed Settings loads. Countdown stops immediately on logical close, exiting DOM is inert and temporary, animations/listeners clean up, and reduced motion settles instantly. Module-only Settings prewarm is delayed, visibility-aware and cancellable, with no forced idle deadline; it trades loading the separate Settings chunk after idle for less first-click work but does not mount hidden UI or start provider effects. The actual measured latency fix bypasses React.lazy's initial fulfilled-promise suspension: five fresh-context local-browser samples improved settled first-visible medians from 343/367 ms to 29/47 ms in Chromium/WebKit. These are fixture timings, not native Windows guarantees. No dependencies, provider polling, thread-loading or streaming changes. Exact measured limits with no extra headroom.

reviewedExceptions.change: Unify model catalog refresh controls across all providers
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 492 Safari / 534 Chrome startup JavaScript bytes for a shared accessible refresh header, OpenAI loading/error state and atomic paginated refresh, and picker-local Cursor errors. Removing duplicated refresh markup and obsolete Cursor header CSS reduces startup CSS by 951 bytes on both targets, so combined raw startup JS plus CSS decreases by 459 Safari / 417 Chrome bytes. No dependencies, timers, background polling, provider restarts or thread/streaming changes. This is UI-feature overhead, not a runtime speed claim. Exact measured limits with no extra headroom; app-entry and CSS limits ratchet down.

reviewedExceptions.change: Provider usage dashboard and bounded OpenRouter cost receipts
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 3,991 Safari / 3,853 Chrome startup JavaScript bytes for frozen provider subtotals, launch pricing status, background metadata attribution and deduplicated cost receipts. Removing obsolete usage styles saves 1,105 startup CSS bytes on both targets; combined raw startup JS plus CSS grows 2,886 / 2,748 bytes. The dashboard and its CSS stay in the deferred Settings chunk, unmount when Settings closes, use no chart dependency, read no transcripts and update only on batched ledger writes. Receipts use one aggregate and at most 1,000 recent ids, not one ledger record per request. Native observation forwards original chunks, caps a candidate frame at 256 KiB and skips JSON parsing on text-only frames. No new polling or generation lookup requests. futures-util was already a transitive Rust dependency; no additional resolved package or frontend dependency is introduced. This is reviewed feature overhead, not a speed improvement claim. Exact measured limits, no extra headroom; app-entry/CSS limits ratchet down.

reviewedExceptions.change: Show provider-native context compaction in thread history
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 2,477 Safari / 2,331 Chrome startup JavaScript bytes for provider-gated Codex lifecycle routing, durable Claude boundary markers, exact timeline ordering and completed-turn visibility. The animated marker adds no startup CSS because its 2.0 KB stylesheet follows the already-lazy ChatTimeline chunk. It adds no polling, provider requests, timers, dependencies or transcript rewriting; OpenRouter and LM Studio are explicitly excluded in live and restored paths. Total JavaScript grows 3,596 / 3,439 bytes, mostly in the lazy renderer and shared persistence presentation logic. This is reviewed UI-feature overhead, not an efficiency claim. Exact measured limits with no extra headroom.

reviewedExceptions.change: Harden compaction ordering, recovery and accessible presentation
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 703 Safari / 621 Chrome startup JavaScript bytes for event-boundary delta flushing, replay deduplication, terminal-state cleanup and truthful restored lifecycle states. Total JavaScript grows 655 / 573 bytes; startup CSS is unchanged and the narrow-layout styling remains lazy. This is a reviewed correctness tradeoff, not a performance improvement: it adds no dependencies, polling, provider requests or timers, and flushes only at compaction boundaries. Exact measured limits without extra headroom.

reviewedExceptions.change: Show native Claude compaction progress with durable lifecycle correlation
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 2,401 Safari / 2,150 Chrome startup and total JavaScript bytes for Claude start/reset/boundary handling, replay-safe identities retained on each compaction row, neutral unconfirmed outcomes, and crash-safe history restoration. Startup CSS is unchanged; the existing lazy marker stylesheet grows 65 bytes. No dependencies, provider requests, polling, hooks or timers are added. Correlation scans only the retained thread activities at lifecycle events, not streaming deltas, and its small persisted metadata is included in transcript memory estimates. This is reviewed feature/correctness overhead rather than an efficiency claim. Limits equal measured production output with no extra headroom.

reviewedExceptions.change: Surface Claude turns that finish without a response
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 797 Safari / 760 Chrome startup and total JavaScript bytes to recover a result-only final answer when possible and otherwise preserve a visible failed-turn diagnostic instead of silently reporting completion. The check is constant-time at the existing result boundary using current-turn task metadata and the final timeline entries; it adds no transcript scans, streaming-path work, retries, dependencies, provider requests, polling, timers or CSS. Avoiding automatic retry prevents duplicate tool side effects. This is reviewed correctness overhead, not an efficiency claim. Exact measured limits without extra headroom.

reviewedExceptions.change: Add GPT-6 Astra identity and an animated astral effort slider
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 382 Safari / Chrome startup JavaScript bytes and 8,072 Safari / 7,869 Chrome startup CSS bytes for Astra's live-catalog identity, generated transparent model artwork, sub-agent fallbacks, five-level palette, drifting nebula, sparse star field, masked two-ribbon astral swell, star thumb, light-theme contrast and complete reduced-motion treatment. The 32 KB icon is a static asset rather than bundled startup code. Settings-only preview CSS remains in the existing lazy Settings stylesheet. Animation is selected-style-only CSS with no JavaScript timers, per-frame React state, canvas, dependencies, provider work, thread data or persistence cost; all decorative layers ignore pointer input. This is reviewed visual-feature overhead, not an efficiency claim. Exact measured limits without extra headroom.

reviewedExceptions.change: Fix the Astra rail loop, make its astral ribbons visible, and drift stars off the selected Astra logo
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 205 Safari / Chrome startup and total JavaScript bytes and 1,645 Safari / 1,623 Chrome startup CSS bytes to repair three defects in the shipped Astra treatment and finish its identity. The nebula now tiles at a fixed width whose first and last stops are the same color and drifts exactly one tile per cycle, replacing a 260%-wide gradient that travelled 140px short of its own tile and snapped once per revolution. The ribbons are explicitly sized ellipses instead of `closest-side` ellipses anchored on an edge, which resolved to a zero radius and painted two layers of nothing. The trigger's star field is six absolutely positioned, aria-hidden, pointer-transparent elements with per-child directions, lifetimes and negative delays. No JavaScript timers, per-frame React state, canvas, dependencies, provider work, thread data or persistence cost; the JavaScript delta is the six static elements on one branch, the emitter is scoped to the selected Astra trigger so menu rows render none, and every added layer is out of flow and ignores pointer input, leaving layout, hit targets and the accessibility tree unchanged. All new motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion, with the stars resting at their invisible base state rather than frozen mid-flight. This is reviewed correctness-and-visual overhead, not an efficiency claim. Exact measured limits without extra headroom.

reviewedExceptions.change: Rework the Astra slider: original palette on a seamless loop, ribbons as stroked sine waves bounded by the effort, a drift that is never re-timed, and visible sparks off the selected logo
reviewedExceptions.decision: Accept 3,985 Safari / 3,963 Chrome startup CSS bytes and 73 Safari / Chrome startup and total JavaScript bytes to fix how the Astra slider reads. The rail returns to the shipped palette's deep-navy anchor on a band 520px wide, so roughly a third of the ramp is on screen at once and the colour reads as a slow journey rather than a short pattern recycling; closing the ramp back to its first colour and travelling exactly one tile per cycle keeps that from snapping, which the browser spec asserts and a paused-animation pixel comparison puts at a mean channel difference of 0.06 across the wrap against 29 for ordinary quarter-cycle motion. Each ribbon becomes one stroked sine path in an inline SVG data URI drawn behind the bar, replacing two tiled blurred ellipses: the weave is now the bar occluding a continuous curve rather than a blur, and the pair counter-drift so their crossings migrate instead of the pattern sliding as one sheet. The ribbons are also masked to the selected effort, reading the same fill custom property the colored bar reads so they end where the color does instead of weaving on across the unfilled remainder; both inner mask stops are clamped with min and max, and an explicit zero-fill rail state hides the decoration where WebKit retains a mixed-unit fallback stop. The added bytes are the two data URIs, their light-theme-neutral rules, and that cross-engine zero-fill safeguard. Still selected-style-only CSS with no JavaScript timers, per-frame React state, canvas, dependencies, provider work, thread data or persistence cost; the data URIs are inline images that need no network request, both layers stay out of flow and ignore pointer input, so layout, hit targets and the accessibility tree are unchanged, and all motion still stops under prefers-reduced-motion with the ribbons resting in place. The matching Settings preview card is fixed the same way and stays in the lazy Settings stylesheet, off the startup path. The drift is also never re-timed any more. Changing animation-duration does not ease an animation's speed: elapsed time is kept and progress is recomputed against the new duration, so the drift lands on a different phase, by an amount that grows with floor(elapsed / duration) and is therefore invisible on a freshly loaded rail and severe on one left on screen. The cycle was derived from --effort-heat, which the rail republishes on every pointer frame of a drag and again on every effort change, so it was re-timed constantly; measured on a two-minute-old rail it threw the nebula 371px and the ribbons 60px in the single frame the thumb was grabbed, and the same on release and on any effort click, against about 0.5px of genuine drift. Both cycles are now plain constants that nothing can rewrite, which takes all three of those to 0.5px or less, and effort still drives the rail's color, glow, tick colors and how far the ribbons reach. To calm the rail while the user aims, dragging pauses the two drifting layers through animation-play-state, which keeps the animation's current time so pause and resume are both seamless, where a duration change can never alter speed without also moving the animation to a new phase; the star field keeps breathing so the rail stays alive. This is one dragging-only rule and two constants, with no new element, script or listener — the dragging class already existed. The same heat-driven-duration pattern remains in the tide, dart and coil styles and is deliberately left alone here. The selected model's trigger logo also sheds visible sparks: the emitter shipped as six 3px dots painted flat in the accent color, effectively invisible against the trigger, and is now nine particles carrying a bright core clipped to a four-point star with a drop-shadow glow, chosen over box-shadow because a box-shadow is drawn on the border box and clipped away with it. Drift and twinkle are split across the element and its ::before so neither keyframe list restates the other's transform and their opacities multiply into a flicker; the light scheme swaps the core to a deep violet with one tight halo and a shallower twinkle, since a dimmed dark core on a white trigger reads as a smudge rather than a dim light. The particle centers and early-flight offsets are precomputed rather than using newer CSS typed arithmetic, preserving the treatment on the Safari 13 and Chromium 105 compatibility targets. The JavaScript delta is the three added decorative elements and the zero-fill rail class, with no timers, per-frame state or persistence, out of flow, pointer-transparent and aria-hidden, and stopped under prefers-reduced-motion at their invisible rest state. This is reviewed visual-correctness overhead, not an efficiency claim. Exact measured limits without extra headroom.
